reasons.no-criterion: The guideline gives no enforcement criterion: it is a principle or process rule.
reasons.incomplete: The guideline's own Enforcement section is incomplete ("???").
reasons.not-enforceable: The guideline itself says the rule cannot be enforced mechanically.
reasons.semantic: Needs type, data-flow or whole-program information that a syntax-level analysis does not have (the optional clang-tidy bridge covers part of it).
reasons.unreliable: The guideline itself calls the proposed check unreliable, or leaves the criterion or its threshold undefined.
reasons.superseded: Superseded by C++20 (rewritten comparison operators, concepts): enforcing it would contradict C++20.
reasons.contradictory: Its enforcement hints contradict another rule, so the verdict depends on information the source does not contain.
reasons.build: Concerns build configuration, tooling or process rather than source code.
reasons.non-rule: A myth / FAQ entry that is not a rule.

notes.C.2: Interpreted as public *data* members: a class whose data members are all public (and nothing is private) should be a struct.
notes.C.8: A struct with any private or protected member (data or function) is reported; the fix turns it into a class and keeps base-class access and the public section.
notes.C.12: Reported for every const / reference data member unless all copy and move operations are deleted.
notes.C.21: Counts user declarations (including = default / = delete) of the five special members; all or none.
notes.C.31: Detects a constructor that allocates (new) into a raw-pointer member of a class that declares no destructor.
notes.C.43: Stays silent for classes with base classes, because their copyability depends on the bases.
notes.C.45: The fix moves the constants to default member initializers.
notes.C.46: Constructors callable with one argument (including defaulted extras); copy/move and initializer_list constructors are on the positive list.
notes.C.67: A class that introduces a virtual function must delete or hide (non-public) its copy operations.
notes.C.86: Superseded by the C++20 rewritten comparison operators (member operator== is the C++20 idiom).
notes.C.127: Applies to classes without base classes that introduce a virtual function; the fix adds a public virtual defaulted destructor.
notes.C.128: Missing override is detected for base classes defined in the same file.
notes.C.132: Reported only for classes whose every member function is virtual and has an implementation.
notes.C.138: Reported for base classes defined in the same file when the derived class hides base overloads without a using-declaration.
notes.C.161: Only the symmetric arithmetic/bitwise operators are checked; comparisons follow the C++20 rules.
notes.C.164: All non-explicit conversion operators (including operator bool).
notes.E.15: Catching by value is reported for every class type, not only for types with a virtual function.
notes.E.31: Uses a small table of the std::exception hierarchy plus classes defined in the same file.
notes.ES.10: For-statement initializers are reported but not auto-fixed.
notes.ES.20: Builtin types and pointers only (types with constructors are not reported); arrays (buffers) are not reported.
notes.ES.22: Detects an uninitialized declaration immediately followed by its first assignment.
notes.ES.27: Variable-length arrays and bounds that are not local constants.
notes.ES.34: Definitions of C-style variadic functions, <cstdarg> and va_* usage.
notes.ES.41: Bitwise operators mixed with other binary operators, and assignments that are not the leftmost operator.
notes.ES.42: Pointer arithmetic on pointer variables and non-constant indexing of C arrays / std::array declared in the same file.
notes.ES.43: Operands that modify and use the same variable (&&, || and ?: are sequenced and excluded).
notes.ES.44: A variable modified in one argument and used in another.
notes.ES.45: Numeric and character literals; the positive list is configurable (cpp20Guidelines.magicConstants.allowList). A literal that is the whole initializer of a variable counts as named.
notes.ES.46: Floating point to integral and long to char, for variables whose declared type is known.
notes.ES.47: NULL, and 0 used as a pointer in initializers, assignments, comparisons and returns.
notes.ES.48: reinterpret_cast is reported here; C-style and functional casts are reported through ES.49 / ES.64.
notes.ES.60: Resource-management functions are: constructors, destructors, operator new/delete, assignment operators, reset and release.
notes.ES.63: Slicing is reported for classes with data members that have derived classes in the same file.
notes.ES.64: Functional casts of builtin types (a class name cannot be told apart from a function without type information).
notes.ES.70: A chain of at least three branches comparing the same variable with literals.
notes.ES.71: Index loops over container[i] and begin()/end() iterator loops whose body only visits the elements.
notes.ES.73: The initializer/increment shares no identifier with the condition, or both are absent.
notes.ES.78: A case that falls through without break/return/throw/continue/goto, [[fallthrough]] or a noreturn call.
notes.ES.79: Enumerations defined in the same file; the fix adds the missing cases.
notes.ES.87: Comparisons with nullptr, true and false in conditions; integer comparisons with 0 are not redundant.
notes.ES.100: Declared signed vs unsigned variables, and signed variables against .size() / sizeof (ptrdiff_t is allowed, as the guideline says); the fix uses std::ssize.
notes.F.2: Reports functions with more than cpp20Guidelines.thresholds.maxParameters (default 6: the guideline calls 7 or more suspicious).
notes.F.3: Limits come from the guideline text: 60 lines, 140 columns, 10 logical paths (a switch counts as one). All configurable.
notes.F.9: Named parameters that are never used in the function (a parameter marked [[maybe_unused]] is accepted).
notes.F.16: Cheap builtin/view types passed by reference to const, std::array above 4 pointers by value, and moved references; class sizes are not known.
notes.F.18: X&& parameters (X not a template parameter) that are never passed to std::move.
notes.F.19: Forwarding references that are used other than as std::forward<T>(x), or forwarded twice on one path.
notes.F.21: std::pair / std::tuple return types (variadic templates are exempt).
notes.F.24: A pointer parameter followed by an integral parameter that is count-named, or whose body indexes the pointer and bounds a loop by the count.
notes.F.43: Returning &local, a local array, or a local by reference.
notes.F.47: Assignment operators (including compound) must return T&.
notes.F.50: A named, capture-less, non-generic lambda at namespace scope.
notes.F.51: Overloads whose parameter list is a prefix of another overload.
notes.F.53: By-reference captures of locals in a lambda that is returned or handed to a thread/async.
notes.F.54: A [=] default capture together with this or a data member.
notes.F.56: Redundant else after a branch that always jumps, and a function whose whole body is one if.
notes.I.2: Non-const variables at namespace scope, and const pointers to non-const data.
notes.I.4: void* parameters or returns, and more than one bool parameter.
notes.I.12: Only with cpp20Guidelines.gsl.enabled: a pointer parameter checked against nullptr (or asserted) on entry.
notes.NL.4: Mixed tabs and spaces (reported once per file, with a whole-file fix) and block contents/closing braces not at the file's indentation step.
notes.NL.9: ALL_CAPS names that are not macros; single-letter template parameters are not names in this sense.
notes.NL.10: Names with camelCase humps. Types are Capitalized_with_underscores (e.g. My_map), everything else lower_case_with_underscores; a leading m_ or trailing _ on members is accepted.
notes.NL.11: Digit sequences with at least cpp20Guidelines.thresholds.digitSeparatorMinDigits digits (guideline: maybe 7).
notes.NL.15: No spaces inside <> of includes, before ; and , or [ , between a function name and ( , inside ( ) and [ ], and no runs of spaces between tokens (alignment before a trailing comment is tolerated).
notes.NL.16: public before protected before private, each once; types, then constructors/assignment/destructor, then functions, then data. The private section is exempt.
notes.NL.17: K&R/Stroustrup: function brace on its own line; class/struct and statement braces on the head's line; a space after if/for/while/switch/catch; branches and bodies on separate lines; case labels aligned with switch; types capitalized, functions not. A cuddled `} else {` is not checked (the guideline does not specify it).
notes.NL.18: T* p / T& r: the declarator operator attaches to the type.
notes.NL.20: Sibling statements or declarations sharing a line.
notes.NL.26: `T const` is reported; `const T` is the conventional notation.
notes.NL.27: Accepted suffixes are configurable: sources .cpp .cxx .cc .C, headers .h .hh .hpp .hxx.
notes.Per.11: Narrow definition: a function over builtin parameters whose only statement returns an expression of its parameters and literals.
notes.R.11: new/delete outside resource-management functions; placement new is exempt.
notes.R.13: More than one new/malloc in one statement.
notes.R.20: new assigned to a raw pointer (gsl::owner<T*> is accepted); the fix converts to std::make_unique.
notes.SF.2: Positive list from the guideline plus C++17 inline variables.
notes.SF.4: Includes after the first declaration (preprocessor directives and comments may precede them).
notes.SF.8: #pragma once is NOT accepted (the guideline says it is non-standard); the guard name is derived from the last two path components.
notes.SF.12: Only a quoted include of a standard header is detected; the filesystem is not consulted.
notes.SL.con.1: C arrays declared in a function or class that also declares an STL container.
notes.SL.io.3: <cstdio> and the printf family; simple printf/fprintf calls are converted to std::format.
notes.T.10: Unconstrained type parameters of non-variadic templates and unconstrained auto parameters (also reports I.9); the quick fixes offer standard concepts.
notes.T.43: typedef; simple typedefs are converted automatically.
notes.T.61: Member types of class templates that do not use every template parameter.
notes.T.143: size() compared with 0/1 and iterators compared with <.
notes.CP.25: std::thread is reported and std::jthread is proposed (C++20 prevails over gsl::joining_thread).

extension.CPP20.suppress: The suppression comment itself: it needs a known rule id and a justification (answer 7A).
extension.CPP20.concepts: std::enable_if / SFINAE replaced by requires clauses (replaces T.48 for C++20).
extension.CPP20.ranges: std::algorithm(c.begin(), c.end(), ...) replaced by the constrained std::ranges algorithm.
extension.CPP20.spaceship: operator!= next to operator==, and groups of relational operators, replaced by operator<=>.
extension.CPP20.nodiscard: Const accessors (and pure free functions in headers) marked [[nodiscard]].
extension.CPP20.bit_cast: memcpy / reinterpret_cast type punning replaced by std::bit_cast.
extension.CPP20.erase_if: The erase-remove idiom replaced by std::erase / std::erase_if.
extension.CPP20.contains: find() != end() replaced by contains(); find(x) == 0 replaced by starts_with().
extension.CPP20.type_traits: Trait<T>::value and ::type replaced by the _v / _t variable and alias templates.
extension.CPP20.removed: Facilities removed or deprecated by C++17/20 (auto_ptr, random_shuffle, bind1st, result_of, register, ...).
extension.CPP20.gsl_to_std: GSL entities that have a standard equivalent (gsl::span, joining_thread, byte, index, narrow_cast).
extension.CPP20.string_view: Read-only const std::string& parameters replaced by std::string_view (only when every use is string_view-compatible).
extension.CPP20.numbers: M_PI and friends replaced by std::numbers.
extension.CPP20.modules: Opt-in (cpp20Guidelines.modules.enforce): #include of standard headers replaced by import.
